subject: Cross-border private-deploy activation criteria & egress policy check-in
messages:
From: Julia Lee <julia.lee@sakura-bank.co.jp>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Sakura Bank Ops <sakura-ops@sakura-bank.co.jp>
Date: Sat, 8 May 2027 00:12:00 +0900
Subject: [Sakura] Questions on activation criteria + egress lock for EU<->APAC private deploy

Hannah —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We reviewed the proposed private deployment model and have a few immediate asks before we sign off on the activation window:

- We need a short, concrete list of activation prerequisites (network, KMS, routing) that our infra team can validate during the prep window.
- Confirm whether egress can be strictly limited to Sakura-owned transit IPs in Tokyo (we cannot allow general outbound to AWS/eu regions).
- If failover to EU is triggered, what telemetry is collected and how long are request logs retained in the failover region?

Can you send a one-pager and any diagrams we can circulate to procurement and compliance? We’d like to lock the activation date by next Tuesday.

Julia
IT Risk & Cloud Ops
Sakura Financial Services

Attachments: none
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Julia Lee <julia.lee@sakura-bank.co.jp>
Cc: Sakura Bank Ops <sakura-ops@sakura-bank.co.jp>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 8 May 2027 02:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: [Sakura] Questions on activation criteria + egress lock for EU<->APAC private deploy

Julia — thanks for the quick note. High level answers first, then I’ll loop in the infra/network owners with a draft checklist and diagrams.

- Activation prerequisites (short):
  1) VPC peering + BGP sessions established between Sakura transit and Redwood private VPC (IP ranges exchanged and ACLs agreed).
  2) KMS envelope keys provisioned: Sakura must provide the public key ID for BYOK; we provide the KMS-usage policy.
  3) Egress policy configured on the private cluster to restrict outbound to specific Sakura-managed CIDR blocks (both Tokyo and EU proxies if used).
  4) Test workloads and synthetic traffic run for 30 minutes during the prep window; latency and token-throughput acceptance criteria signed off.
  5) Rollback play and authorization contacts listed in the activation runbook.

- Egress: yes — we can lock to Sakura-owned transit IPs and to an allowlist of destination FQDNs. We will not route general internet egress from the private cluster; only explicit outbound to your proxies.

- Logs during failover: we keep request logs and token-level traces in the active region only by default. For the failover window we can enable short-term cross-region replication of request logs for troubleshooting — retention in the failover region can be limited to a configured window (default 7 days, configurable down to 24 hours for sensitive accounts). We will record the exact telemetry fields we replicate.

Next steps: Karthik / Marcus — can you review the checklist and attach a network diagram we can share with Sakura this morning? I’ve started a one-pager (attached) — sending in the next message with diagrams.

— Hannah
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachment: activation_criteria_v1.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Julia Lee <julia.lee@sakura-bank.co.jp>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 8 May 2027 10:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: [Sakura] Questions on activation criteria + egress lock for EU<->APAC private deploy

Julia / team — short technical clarifications and proposed constraints from the networking side. I’ve attached a rough zone map (network-egress-zones.drawio) and a KMS mapping matrix.

1) Egress model options (we recommend Option B below for strict residency):
  Option A — Transit NAT: Redwood NATs egress through our managed proxies in each region; allowlisting by destination IP possible but requires Redwood-managed proxies (not ideal for Sakura).
  Option B — Customer-provided egress proxies (recommended): Sakura’s transit accepts outbound only to Sakura-owned proxies (Tokyo and Amsterdam). Redwood routes outbound via BGP-advertised next-hops; egress lockdown enforced via cluster-level egress policies.
  Option C — Private-interconnect-only (most restrictive): No public egress; only Sakura-owned peering endpoints permitted. This needs private interconnect and strict ACL enforcement on both sides.

2) Failover ordering and data residency behavior:
  - On a planned EU failover, active session state will be primarized in the EU cluster. We will keep ephemeral KV caches in region and only ship request logs if you opt-in.
  - Unplanned failover (auto): we recommend a short cool-down (2–5 minutes) before cross-region routing to avoid split-brain where clients hit both regions.

3) KMS / key custody:
  - For BYOK we need Sakura to create per-region key aliases and share the key ARNs; Redwood will never export plaintext key material. The KMS matrix explains per-region usage and rotation windows.

Open question for Sakura: do you want cross-region log replication for debugging (short retention) or strict single-region retention during normal ops? Please confirm.

Attachments: network-egress-zones.drawio, kms-keymap_matrix.xlsx

--
Karthik Iyer
Staff Network Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Julia Lee <julia.lee@sakura-bank.co.jp>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 16:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: [Sakura] Questions on activation criteria + egress lock for EU<->APAC private deploy

Julia / Hannah / team — compliance read here. A few clarifying constraints from SOC- and data-residency perspective: 

- If Sakura requires write-only encryption keys per-region (i.e., Sakura-managed keys with no replication), we need an explicit policy that outlines key usage and confirmed key policies from your KMS team. That’s one of the go/no-go items for our security checklist.
- Short-term cross-region log replication for failover debugging is acceptable if: 1) logs are pseudonymized for PII, 2) retention is bounded (we suggest 72 hours by default), and 3) replication is auditable in the activation runbook.
- Please provide a completed network ACL export (simple CSV) with the exact CIDRs you will advertise so we can validate there are no overlapping ranges with our internal infra.

I’ve attached a quick SOC evidence pointer file listing the documents we’ll need at hand during the activation review. If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute tabletop tomorrow to walk through sign-off items.

Thanks — Olga
Head of Compliance, Privacy & Controls
Redwood Inference

Attachments: soc2-evidence-links.txt
